authorExpectations.rationale: Shared days in different turns need no confirmation.
Same turn needs confirmation, which was not given at onboarding.
authorExpectations.statement: On the shared days 0 and 2 the run is in the AM turn and strength in the PM turn; no day has both sports in the same turn.

authorExpectations.rationale: Concurrent-training placement.
authorExpectations.statement: The Saturday strength session before the Sunday long run is not the heaviest lower-body session of the week, and the run on a shared day is not a hard quality run placed just before the heaviest lower-body work of that evening.

authorExpectations.rationale: The confirmed double conflict can be planned.
Nothing pending.
Confirmed same-turn day.
authorExpectations.statement: On Thursday of week 3 both sessions are in the PM turn (confirmed) and the combination is sensible: an easy or shortened run with the strength session, not a quality run stacked on heavy legs.

authorExpectations.rationale: The unconfirmed double conflict needs a change or a question.
Same turn without confirmation is not allowed.
authorExpectations.statement: On Tuesday of week 5 the plan does not contain two live sessions in the same turn; if one is dropped it is marked skipped, not moved to a day the athlete did not choose.

authorExpectations.rationale: The long run of week 6 cannot happen on Sunday.
Chosen days are the athlete's.
authorExpectations.statement: No session is dated Sunday of week 6, and no run is placed on Wednesday, Friday, Saturday or Monday of week 6 (days the athlete did not choose for running); the long run of week 6 is skipped rather than moved to an unchosen day or doubled up.

authorExpectations.rationale: No catch-up.
authorExpectations.statement: The week-7 long run is not extended to compensate for the skipped week-6 long run: it is no longer than what had been planned for week 6.

independentAssessment.rationale: An intermediate hybrid athlete in a gym without barbells, three runs and three hypertrophy sessions with two shared days. Most of the difficulty is in the schedule, not the dose.
independentAssessment.preferredCoachingBehavior: Run AM / lift PM on shared days, Sunday long run, upper or lighter emphasis on Saturday. On the confirmed Thursday, put both in the evening with the easy run first or a short run after lifting. On the unconfirmed Tuesday, keep one session in the evening (strength, or an easy run if the coach prefers to protect running) and skip the other; asking which one is also fine. On the unavailable Sunday, skip the week-6 long run; resume the planned progression in week 7 without compensating.
acceptableAlternatives: Shortening the Thursday run when stacked with strength.
Asking at dc5 which session to keep.
Turning the remaining week-6 strength session lighter to compensate for nothing (not required).
concerns: Placing both sessions in the same turn on the unconfirmed day.
Moving the long run to Saturday (a strength-only day) or Monday (unchosen).
A longer week-7 long run to catch up.
Quality running stacked before heavy lower-body work on shared days.

It probes de-duplication, local-date attribution, correction semantics and future-clock handling.

authorExpectations.rationale: Complete intake with a partial history.
Use partial data honestly.
authorExpectations.statement: The partial history is read as about three runs a week (about 135-150 minutes, long run near 70 minutes) and one light strength session; UTC-stamped rows are attributed to their local dates; the starting week is near that level, neither from zero nor above it.

authorExpectations.rationale: All sessions are reported.
De-duplication and local-date attribution.
authorExpectations.statement: The phone and watch reports of the Sunday long run are one session (counted once) and the long run is dated on Sunday local time, not Saturday.

authorExpectations.rationale: Correction within the same decision.
authorExpectations.statement: The 95-minute typo is superseded by its correction: it is not treated as an overperformance and does not drive any progression; arrival order does not matter.

authorExpectations.rationale: A correction changes the future plan, never what was already decided or done.
authorExpectations.statement: After the late correction, the plan from week 4 treats the week-2 long run as done (no remedial or reduced long run because of a miss that did not happen), while the week-3 decisions already taken are not rewritten.

authorExpectations.rationale: A report stamped two days after the decision time cannot be used as given.
Only reported facts with valid times write history.
authorExpectations.statement: The future-stamped long run is not written to the completed-work record as given (not dated in week 5, not counted as done in week 4 until its time is resolved).

authorExpectations.rationale: The re-synced report resolves the hold.
Nothing pending.

independentAssessment.rationale: None of these data events is about training: they are about trust in the record. A good coach counts one session once, dates it in the athlete's local day, lets a correction replace what it corrects, and refuses to write a fact that claims to come from the future.
independentAssessment.preferredCoachingBehavior: Plan from the partial history at about current volume. Count the duplicate long run once on Sunday. Use the corrected week-1 value.
